summary: Initial discovery for Atlas Pharma private VPC deployment. Main topics: region constraints, VPC peering vs PrivateLink, CIDR overlap, cross-account networking, required endpoints/ports, KMS/encryption, SOC2/compliance. Agreed to share diagrams and schedule technical deep-dive.
transcript:
00:00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick rollcall?
00:00:07 - Priya: Priya here, CTO at Atlas.
00:00:10 - Claire: Claire, infra.
00:00:12 - Rajesh: Rajesh, security.
00:00:14 - Luis: Luis, DevOps.
00:00:16 - Maya: Great, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and Samir's our solutions engineer. Samir do you want to intro?
00:00:25 - Samir: Yep hi all, Samir Rao, backend/infra for Redwood, I've been doing Private deployments and VPC integrations.
00:00:32 - Maya: Goal for today is to understand Atlas's network constraints, region requirements, and any security gating that would affect a Private/VPC deployment. we'll cover peering, endpoints, and KMS.
00:00:45 - Priya: High level: we're looking to move certain inference workloads off hosted into a Private deployment due to PHI concerns and data residency for EU patients. timeline is Q3 pilot then broader in Q4 if all good.
00:00:58 - Maya: Got it. is the pilot purely in AWS or multi-cloud?
00:01:03 - Claire: AWS first. we have accounts in eu-west-1 and us-east-1, but the data must stay eu-west-1 for patient data. That said, some orchestration services run in us-east-1.
00:01:15 - Samir: That maps well to our typical setup. we can region pin a Private deployment to eu-west-1. question: do you plan cross-region peering or a local-only footprint?
00:01:28 - Priya: Local only ideally for PHI. but we may need a control-plane connection to our us-east-1 management account. what does Redwood need for the control plane?
00:01:38 - Samir: For Private we usually have a customer-managed network where our runtime sits in your VPC or a peered account. we support a few patterns: VPC peering, AWS Transit Gateway, or PrivateLink/Interface endpoints. control plane traffic can be over a private VPC endpoint or, if you prefer, we can do a limited egress to Redwood backend through NAT but many enterprise customers prefer PrivateLink.
00:02:02 - Rajesh: Security question: we require no public internet egress for PHI workloads. all outbound must go through our proxy and to specific internal IP ranges. can Redwood's runtime operate fully without public egress?
00:02:14 - Samir: Yes, runtime can be configured to avoid public egress. we'll need either interface endpoints for required AWS services or a peering arrangement. there are some background callbacks (metrics/tracing) — those can be routed to your logging endpoints.
00:02:28 - Luis: what port/ips are needed? our networking team needs a list.
00:02:31 - Samir: we'll provide a port list in the runbook. common ones: outbound 443 for control plane if using PrivateLink, health checks over TCP ephemeral, and optionally 22 for support-only when you open a ticket — but that's not required. also we use internal RPC between nodes over a set of ephemeral ports.
00:02:47 - Maya: we'll share a checklist. Claire, do you have restrictions on creating interface endpoints in your account? sometimes security blocks that.
00:02:55 - Claire: We generally allow endpoints but need approval from network. Also CIDR overlap is a concern — our VPC is 10.1.0.0/16 already.
00:03:02 - Samir: We can deploy into a dedicated VPC in your account or use peering from a Redwood-managed account. if you have CIDR overlap we usually recommend Transit Gateway or using non-overlapping subnets in a dedicated VPC.
00:03:14 - Priya: Do you support cross-account VPC peering?
00:03:18 - Samir: Yes cross-account peering is supported. peering requires symmetric routing config and sometimes additional route propagation with TGW. for scale and multi-VPC setups Transit Gateway reduces management overhead.
00:03:32 - Rajesh: KMS — we must manage the keys. can Redwood integrate with our KMS/HSM?
00:03:36 - Samir: Yes. We support customer-managed KMS keys for data at rest. for certain on-prem HSM setups we have partners but for AWS KMS you're able to provide a key policy that grants Redwood the decrypt/encrypt permissions limited to the Redwood service principal. we also support bringing-your-own-HSM via CloudHSM in some configs, but that'll be part of an enterprise plan.
00:03:57 - Priya: Good. any SOC2 or audit logs we get?
00:04:01 - Maya: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we'll share the report under NDA. plus the Private deployment produces audit logs which can be forwarded to your CloudWatch/Elasticsearch or to a S3 bucket.
00:04:12 - Rajesh: We need to validate that logs include model version, user request id, and token counts for billing reconciliation.
00:04:19 - Samir: We emit request tracing with model_id and request_id. token accounting is in our cost telemetry. we'll work with you on the schema.
00:04:28 - Luis: latency — if we go intra-region eu-west-1 what latency should we expect for typical 2k token calls?
00:04:34 - Samir: depends on model size and GPU. for a medium-sized model on dedicated infra we typically see p95 ~ 80-250ms per chunk; end-to-end for 2k tokens may be a few seconds depending on batch/streaming. we can run benchmark in your VPC to give exact numbers.
00:04:50 - Priya: Cost is big for us. we need to compare dedicated vs hosted. any guidance on unit economics for Private dedicated?
00:04:58 - Maya: Private ded (reserved capacity) does have a higher upfront commit but predictable unit cost and data isolation. hosted has lower barrier to entry but not acceptable for PHI per your compliance. we'll send a pricing sketch for pilot vs projected monthly for steady 100 rps.
00:05:14 - Claire: Region question: we only want eu-west-1 for data plane. is it ok if control plane lives elsewhere if it's just management telemetry?
00:05:21 - Samir: yes but we can also offer a Private control plane in your VPC for enterprise customers if you require zero cross-region control plane. otherwise we do minimal control-plane calls to a regional endpoint; it's configurable.
00:05:35 - Rajesh: We also need RBAC/SAML integration and granular role separation. can we map to IdP groups?
00:05:41 - Maya: We support SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC with roles. Samir can walk through what levels of access are available.
00:05:50 - Samir: From infra perspective we distinguish: admin, ops, read-only, and service accounts. we also support audit-only service accounts for metrics.
00:05:58 - Luis: about onboarding — what's the sequence? how long to get a pilot up?
00:06:02 - Maya: Typical pilot is 2-4 weeks after we get networking info and any required access. includes a small dedicated cluster, test keys, and benching.
00:06:10 - Claire: For peering we need account IDs and CIDR ranges. we'll share that.
00:06:14 - Priya: Any blockers you're seeing now?
00:06:16 - Samir: nothing major. the usual ones are CIDR overlap and private endpoint policy in your org. Also sometimes compliance requires a dedicated control plane which adds time.
00:06:25 - Rajesh: We'd like encryption-in-transit end-to-end. TLS is fine, but do you do mutual TLS for service-to-service?
00:06:33 - Samir: We support mutual TLS for inter-service and can do client certs for especially sensitive comms. we'll document the cert rotation process.
00:06:41 - Maya: Quick note on troubleshooting: if you want support-level access we can do temporary bastion with limited time window and audited sessions, otherwise we use logs and metrics.
00:06:50 - Luis: ok that works.
00:06:52 - Priya: What about IP address consumption? we are tight on subnets.
00:06:57 - Samir: We try to be IP-efficient, suggest /24 or larger subnets for node pools; we'll provide exact mapping. if you're tight we can also do host-level NAT through your network.
00:07:09 - Maya: i'll recap next steps at the end, but Samir can describe two recommended networking patterns quickly?
00:07:15 - Samir: Sure. Pattern A: Deploy Redwood runtime into a dedicated VPC in your account with interface endpoints for control plane services. Pros: full data residency, no cross-account peering, easier audit. Cons: you manage the VPC and IPs. Pattern B: Peer Redwood-managed VPCs into your account or use Transit Gateway. Pros: less IP management on your side, faster onboarding. Cons: cross-account trust and more network ops to maintain.
00:07:44 - Claire: Transit Gateway sounds reasonable for multi-VPC but may be overkill for a single pilot.
00:07:50 - Maya: we'll include both options in the runbook.
00:07:53 - Luis: What about PrivateLink specifically?
00:07:55 - Samir: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is great for avoiding public internet. we create an NLB in our account and you create an endpoint service or we ask you to create the endpoint for certain service names. might require endpoint policies.
00:08:09 - Priya: Ok. If we proceed, what's the minimum commit?
00:08:13 - Maya: For pilot we can do a short-term evaluation contract with limited nodes — usually month-to-month for pilot. For dedicated production we'll discuss reserved capacity.
00:08:22 - Rajesh: We also need an inventory of what metadata Redwood stores and retention windows.
00:08:27 - Samir: We store request metadata for X days by default; retention is configurable and we can shorten/limit PHI retention. we'll include default retention in the security docs.
00:08:38 - Maya: sounds like the main blockers are: Atlas to share CIDRs/account IDs and Rajesh to confirm KMS/HSM policy. We'll send diagrams and schedule deep-dive. Anything else?
00:08:50 - Claire: Can you include a sample trust policy for KMS? that would speed legal.
00:08:55 - Samir: yes we'll draft that.
00:08:58 - Priya: Let's set the deep-dive for April 21st 1400 CET — does that work for you?
00:09:04 - Maya: works from Redwood side, i'll send calendar invite.
00:09:07 - Luis: thanks all.
00:09:09 - Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and the runbook.

00:09:36 - Samir: reiterating — we can pin to eu-west-1 for data plane and optionally control plane can be regional or private.
00:09:48 - Rajesh: (mutter) need to check DLP with legal.
00:09:55 - Maya: i'll include the DLP controls we support in the security doc.

00:10:20 - Maya: okay that's it, thanks everyone.
